items.name: cleanyourtv
items.description: Debloat any Android or Google TV over Wi-Fi and get an Apple TV-style home.
items.readme:
cleanyour.tv · The prompt · 54 TV lists · 12 built on it · The tweet

Strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, and replace the ad-filled home screen with a clean launcher that looks like an Apple TV. **No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind.**

54 TVs with tested lists  ·  23 brands  ·  12 languages  ·  280 KB launcher

![Before: stock Google TV home with a sponsored ad. After: the Clean Your TV launcher](docs/stock-vs-new-side.jpg) > Vibe coded my parents' TV this afternoon! It was showing a sponsored ad before you could even get > to Netflix. Gave Claude Code the model number, it found the TV on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages > and wrote a new launcher. Looks like an Apple TV now lol. > > [@gathint, 17 October 2026](https://x.com/gathint/status/2111379569030939102). The replies are where > most of the TV lists here came from. The repo was called tv-vibehack until the 19th; old links work. ## How it works Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Switch on USB debugging in the TV's developer options, allow your computer once, and the rest is standard Android tooling: 1. **Back up** the list of installed packages and settings. 2. **Disable** the manufacturer's telemetry, ad services, content rows and preloaded junk with `pm disable-user`. Nothing is uninstalled, so a restore script can undo every step. 3. **Install** a small native launcher and make it the default home screen. The bloat differs by brand, so the prompt has your coding assistant discover it on your TV and ask before touching anything you might use. ## Quick start You need a computer on the same Wi-Fi as the TV and a coding assistant with shell access (Claude Code or similar). | | | |---|---| | **1. On the TV** | Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on **Build** seven times → back → Developer options → **USB debugging** on. If you see a Network or ADB debugging toggle, turn that on too. Keep the TV on. | | **2. On your computer** | Paste [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md) into your assistant and fill in your TV model. | | **3. Follow along** | Accept "Allow USB debugging?" on the TV, then answer the checklist: which apps you use, which four go in the dock, whether to keep the voice assistant, Chromecast and updates. | The assistant backs up, debloats, builds and installs the launcher, and checks each step with screenshots pulled from the TV. With this repo as context it takes about fifteen minutes. ## What you get - **A pitch-black home** with a dock of your four favourite apps in a rounded band, where Apple TV puts it. - **A top shelf** naming the focused app in large type, with an ambient glow in a colour taken from its artwork. - **The rest of your apps in a grid** that slides up when you press Down. - **One floating glass highlight** that springs from tile to tile. The focused tile lifts and shows its name. - **Three frosted buttons**: Inputs (HDMI ports, AV, Live TV), Wi-Fi or Ethernet with the network name, Settings. - **A greeting, a thin clock and the date** in [Outfit](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Outfit), and a matching Clock screensaver. - **Themes** that change colours, wallpaper, dock and columns without a rebuild, and **module cards** that let other apps plug a tile in, only with your say-so. And a TV that stops working against you: no sponsored rows, no "Discover" nags, no analytics phoning home, no apps you never asked for. | | | |---|---| | ![The top shelf names the focused app over an ambient glow in its colour](docs/focus-2-up-netflix.png) | ![The Inputs popup: HDMI ports with what is connected, AV and Live TV](docs/inputs-menu.jpg) | | *Top shelf and ambient glow* | *Inputs: HDMI with connection state, AV, Live TV* | | ![The grid with the glass highlight on a tile and its name beneath](docs/focus-1-fancode.png) | ![The Clock screensaver: a thin clock drifting over the glow](docs/clock-screensaver.png) | | *The grid, one glass highlight, the tile's name* | *Clock screensaver, drifts so nothing burns in* | | ![The aurora theme: a wallpaper and tinted pills, pushed without a rebuild](docs/theme-aurora.jpg) | ![Six columns and a six-app dock from a theme's config.json](docs/theme-six-columns.jpg) | | *Aurora theme, pushed with `tools/theme.sh`* | *Six columns and a six-app dock, same launcher* | ## Supported TVs Anything running **Android TV** or **Google TV**. Samsung (Tizen) and LG (webOS) run different systems; see [SHOWCASE.md](SHOWCASE.md) for a webOS port. **Fire TV** takes the debloat half only, since Fire OS will not hand Home to a third-party launcher. A few China-market TCL sets refuse to install any launcher at all; their lists say so in the header. Tested lists from contributors, one folder per model in [`examples/`](examples/): **Xiaomi** 12 · **TCL** 11 · **Sony** 8 · **CHiQ** 2 · **Hisense** 2 · **Philips** 2 · Amazon Fire TV Stick · BenQ · Chromecast with Google TV · Hitachi · Insignia Fire TV · NVIDIA Shield · OnePlus · Panasonic · RCA · Redmi · SANYO · Skyworth · Thomson · Toshiba Fire TV · Vu · Stellamore and XGIMI projectors

Your TV not here? The prompt discovers the bloat itself. Add your list afterwards and the next person with your model skips that step: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Doing it by hand Everything the assistant does, you can run yourself. The tools need Python 3 and nothing else. ```bash python3 -m venv tools/venv && tools/venv/bin/pip install -r tools/requirements.txt export TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 # your TV's IP address tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --probe # model, Android version, firmware tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py 'pm list packages' # one shell command on the TV tools/disable.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # apply a debloat list tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # undo it, stock launcher back TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 launcher/build-and-install.sh # build the launcher and make it Home tools/theme.sh themes/aurora # push a theme; --reset removes it ``` | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | [`tools/tv.py`](tools/tv.py) | Pure-Python ADB client: shell, batch, push, pull. Works where the stock `adb` binary is blocked. | | [`tools/b64push.py`](tools/b64push.py) | Uploads large files such as APKs in base64 chunks and verifies the checksum. | | [`tools/disable.sh`](tools/disable.sh), [`restore.sh`](tools/restore.sh) | Apply or undo a debloat list. | | [`tools/theme.sh`](tools/theme.sh) | Push a folder from [`themes/`](themes/) to the launcher and restart Home. | | [`launcher/build-and-install.sh`](launcher/build-and-install.sh) | Builds a shrunk release (about 280 KB), installs it, switches Home, and rolls back if Home does not land on it. | Debloat list paths passed to `disable.sh` and `restore.sh` are relative to the directory you run from, so your own lists can live outside the repository. Absolute paths also work. Every script has a PowerShell twin next to it. On Windows with Android Studio installed nothing else is needed: ```powershell python -m venv tools\venv; tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r tools\requirements.txt powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File launcher\build-and-install.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\disable.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 examples\xiaomi-mi-tv-4a\debloat.txt ``` The install scripts ask the TV which launcher owns Home and only disable one they recognise (`tvlauncher` or `launcherx`); pass `STOCK_LAUNCHER=` (`-StockLauncher`) to override, or `none` to leave it alone. ## The launcher A small native Android TV app (`com.gathin.tvhome`, about 280 KB installed) in plain Java with AndroidX RecyclerView and nothing heavier. Built for sets with 1 GB of RAM: no blur, no video, no network, no background services. It needs JDK 17 and Android SDK platform 34 to build; on macOS, `brew install openjdk@17 android-commandlinetools` and `sdkmanager "platforms;android-34" "build-tools;34.0.0"`. On Linux the install script finds `~/Android/Sdk` and the `java` on your PATH. - **Configure** in [`config.xml`](launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml): dock order, hidden apps, the Live TV package, columns (tiles shrink from 5 up), rows under the dock, an optional VPN app for the network pill, and `reduced_motion` for TVs whose GPU cannot keep up. - **Themes** set the same keys plus a background colour and a wallpaper from a `config.json` pushed to the TV, no rebuild. Three ship in [`themes/`](themes/), documented there. - **Language** follows the TV: English, German, Spanish, Catalan, French, Russian, Serbian (Latin), Polish, Arabic, Simplified Chinese, Thai, Turkish. Android 13+ can set it for the launcher alone: `tools/tv.py 'cmd locale set-app-locales com.gathin.tvhome --locales ca'`. Russian includes the module-card approval and management screens and the VPN-off badge. - **Module cards** let any TV app declare its own tile (label, caption, glow). The launcher asks you once per app, Keep hidden by default, and remembers the answer for that app's signing key and card name. Hold OK on Settings to change your mind. How to make one: [`docs/modules.md`](docs/modules.md); the contract: [`docs/specs/card.md`](docs/specs/card.md). - **Clock screensaver**: a drifting clock over the glow, so nothing burns in. Pick "Clock" in the TV's screensaver settings, or over ADB: `tools/tv.py 'settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream; settings put secure screensaver_enabled 1'` - **Remote keys**: an optional accessibility service keeps the remote's Input button working on Google TV (`INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1` at install), another fixes sticks whose Home key sends ALL_APPS and opens Settings from the remote's gear button, even one Android does not map (`HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1`, scancodes in `config.xml`). - **Navigation** is deliberate: Up and Down move one row, the top buttons never fall through to tiles and Down from them returns to the dock tile you came from, the last focused app is remembered, and installing or removing an app refreshes the tiles while Home is open. - **Artwork**: app banners load at xhdpi or better, so low-density TV UIs do not downsample them before the focus zoom. ## Restoring your TV Keep the list you applied. The restore script re-enables exactly those packages, puts the stock launcher back as Home and resets the animation scales: ```bash TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/restore.sh examples//debloat.txt # Android TV TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/restore.sh examples//debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx # Google TV ``` It leaves the new launcher installed (remove it from the TV's Settings → Apps if you want it gone) and does not know about packages you disabled outside the list. To switch back later, run the install script again; it works out which launcher to disable even when Home has fallen back to Android's chooser. If the TV is unreachable, its own Settings → Apps page can re-enable packages too. ## When something goes wrong The full list of things that bit us is in [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). The three that matter most: - **macOS blocks `adb connect`** ("No route to host") under Local Network privacy. `tools/tv.py` avoids the binary. - **Disable the stock launcher only after the new one is installed and running**, or Home lands on a factory test app. The install script orders this for you. - **On Google TV the setup wizard** (`com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith`) can take Home and crash-loop the system after the stock launcher is disabled. Disable it too, and list it in your `debloat.txt` so restore brings it back. Stuck already? `tools/tv.py 'pm enable --user 0 com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx'`. ## Questions people ask **Is this safe? Can it brick the TV?** Nothing is flashed, rooted or deleted; packages are disabled in the user profile. The risk is disabling something the TV leans on, which is why lists are applied in small batches with a restore script ready. The TV's own Settings → Apps page can re-enable packages even without the tools. **What about firmware updates?** Most lists disable the update service, so updates arrive only when you re-enable it. If one lands, the worst case is a package coming back and you re-run the script. **Won't the apps break?** Streaming apps still update through the Play Store, which is left alone. The launcher just lists what is installed and launches it with intents that have been stable for a decade. **Isn't ADB access a security hole?** It is one explicit "allow this computer" tap on the TV, the same as developing an Android app. Switch USB debugging off afterwards; the launcher keeps working. **Can it block ads inside apps too?** Partly, with Android's Private DNS (Android 9 and newer). Point it at an ad-blocking resolver such as [AdGuard DNS](https://adguard-dns.io) and every app's ad and tracker domains stop resolving, system-wide, surviving reboots. The trade-off: that resolver then sees every DNS query the TV makes. ```bash tools/tv.py 'settings put global private_dns_specifier dns.adguard-dns.com' tools/tv.py 'settings put global private_dns_mode hostname' ``` It does not remove YouTube ads, which come from the same servers as the videos. If an app stops playing or the TV reports "No internet" (the resolver is down or unreachable), switch back with `tools/tv.py 'settings put global private_dns_mode opportunistic'`. **AirPlay?** Not from this repo. Chromecast built-in stays for Android phones. For iPhones, [jqssun/android-airplay-server](https://github.com/jqssun/android-airplay-server) works; an install script for it is in [PR #84](https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv/pull/84). **Can I just download the APK?** Build it with the one-line script; it takes a minute and you control what goes on your TV. No prebuilt binaries. ## Contributing The most useful contribution is your TV's debloat list, so the next person with that model does not have to rediscover it. Launcher improvements and sharper prompt wording are welcome too. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the format and the testing we ask for. Built something on top, a launcher, a port, a theme? Add it to [SHOWCASE.md](SHOWCASE.md), where eleven projects already live: a webOS port for LG, a Stremio shelf, a Hisense restyle, Fire TV launchers, an AirPlay installer. The people whose work is in this repo:
Star history

items.description: DeepInfer: High-performance, large-scale inference framework for DeepSeek models
items.readme:
# DeepInfer

DeepInfer is the high-performance inference framework that powers DeepSeek's large-scale production services. This open-source release provides offline inference with the core features needed for serving at scale.

Supported models:

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Supported features:

- Optimized kernels, model and sampler runtime
- Parallelism: Attention DP / balanced CP, MoE EP + EPLB
- DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification
- SWA bounded replay
- Asynchronous scheduling (zero-overhead batch scheduler)
- Batch-invariant inference
- Deterministic sampling
- Structured outputs

<details>
<summary>Feature details and configuration</summary>

- **Optimized kernels:** [FlashMLA](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA), [DeepGEMM](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM), [DeepEP](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP), [TileKernels](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/TileKernels), [DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect), and custom [TileLang kernels](deepinfer/model_executor/layers/tilelang_ops).
- **DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification:** accelerate decoding with draft tokens and use confidence estimates to schedule verification. Set `DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=1`; `DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE` controls the maximum draft length (default: 5).
- **Decoder SWA bounded replay:** reduce decoder prefill work by replaying only a bounded suffix. Set `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_MODE=compact` and `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_KEEP_TOKENS=140` for the default V4.1 settings; the retained suffix must cover the SWA window plus the maximum backtracking length.
- **Asynchronous scheduling:** overlap CPU batch scheduling with device execution. Enabled by default.
- **Batch-invariant inference:** keep model results identical across different batch compositions. Enable with `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (NVIDIA only).
- **Deterministic sampling:** produce identical outputs for identical input tokens and sampling parameters. Set `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=0` and pass a fixed `seq_seed` to `SamplingParams` (NVIDIA only).
- **Structured outputs:** constrain generation to a regex, JSON schema, or EBNF grammar. Pass `so_args={"schema_type": ..., "schema": ...}` to `SamplingParams`; see [examples](examples/_structured_output.py).

</details>

Supported hardware:

- NVIDIA SM100 GPUs
- Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs

Required for a complete inference service (not included in this release):

- A KV cache system
- VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation (most required engine functionality is already implemented)
- Load balancing across data-parallel replicas for both prefill and decode

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- Linux
- GCC >= 13.0
- Python 3.12
- CUDA 13 (NVIDIA only)
- CANN 9.2 (Ascend only)

### Build from source

Before building DeepInfer, please create and activate an empty Python 3.12 environment.

``` bash
# Use `ascend` instead for the Ascend platform
# Keep it exported in the environment where you run DeepInfer
export DEEPINFER_ACCELERATOR=nvidia
./build.sh
```

### Offline inference

The default checkpoint, [`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017), is
downloaded into the Hugging Face cache on the first run; set `DEEPINFER_HF_MODEL_DIR=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` to
run from a local copy instead.

``` bash
python examples/offline_inference.py
```

See [examples](examples/README.md) for details.

## Performance benchmarks

| Prefill | Decode |
| :---: | :---: |
| [![Prefill: non-cached input throughput vs. latency](doc/images/prefill_pareto.png)](doc/images/prefill_pareto.png) | [![Decode: output throughput vs. per-user speed](doc/images/decode_pareto.png)](doc/images/decode_pareto.png) |

Measured on 4 SM100 GPUs for prefill and 64 for decode — each within one scale-up domain. To reproduce the benchmarks, see [run_sweep.sh](examples/sweep/run_sweep.sh).

## Evaluation benchmarks

See [eval/README.md](eval/README.md).

## License

DeepInfer is released under the Apache License 2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

## Acknowledgments

DeepInfer was originally built primarily on [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), with additional inspiration from [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) and [TensorRT-LLM](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM). We thank their developers.

items.description: An agent skill for creating detailed, interactive isometric illustrations of real-world machines and complex systems. Generates polished SVGs with optional WebGL shaders and 3D effects.
items.readme:
Anatomy

A Claude skill that explains an idea by building it as a real, working object.
Crafted, interactive isometric figures with many small precise parts, in SVG, WebGL and 3D.

   

Quick start · Gallery · What it makes · Install · Usage · Examples · How it works · Limits

examples/raptor-engine, light theme, firing. The engine and stand are SVG; the plume is a WebGL shader in the same isometric camera.

--- Ask Claude for a figure that explains a technical idea, and Anatomy has it invent a physical thing whose working *is* the concept. A cache key that skips work when nothing changed becomes a pin-tumbler lock that only turns when every pin matches. One GPU context serving many canvases becomes a gantry plotter whose single print head visits 16 wells. Then Claude builds that thing out of dozens of small, solid, shaded parts, puts it in a framed card with a title, a hint and a live readout, makes it move calmly under the pointer and the keyboard, and checks its own work by zooming in on every joint. Every number the figure shows comes from the same small model that moves its parts. ## Quick start ```sh npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g -a claude-code ``` Then, in Claude Code: ```text /anatomy explain how a token bucket rate limiter works, interactive ``` That's it. No API keys and nothing to `npm install`: the kit uses only Node's built-in modules. ## Gallery
raptor-engine: hover to take it apart into 11 assemblies. An audit proves that no pipe passes through anything, at rest, apart and in every frame between. ripple-tank: SVG apparatus over two WebGL layers (lamp light and caustics on the paper, reflections in the water) driven by a dispersion and optics model.
turning-dial: the 3D mode (beta). About 90 parts are re-projected and re-shaded every frame as you drag the dial. dial-indicator: the smallest example, about 300 lines. Hover to slide the carriage; the needle reads each block.
Every screenshot is the light theme of a page in [`examples/`](examples), captured with the skill's own [`scripts/capture.mjs`](scripts/capture.mjs) and [`scripts/drive.mjs`](scripts/drive.mjs). The built pages are committed: open any `.html` in `examples/` to try it. ## What it makes Three kinds of figure. All three share one kit, one camera and one set of craft rules. | Kind | What it is | Example | |---|---|---| | **SVG** | The core. Solid isometric parts with four-tone shading, painted back to front, in a card with a live readout and eased motion. It ships as a standalone HTML page, a lone `.svg` file with its styles embedded, or React/Next.js components. | `dial-indicator`, `desk-computer`, `arcade-cabinet`, `test-rig` | | **SVG + WebGL** | For what lines can't draw: fire, exhaust, water, caustics, lamp light, glow, steam. The shader runs in a canvas between a back and a front SVG, in the figure's own isometric camera, so it sits inside the drawing. The SVG still reads without WebGL. | `raptor-engine`, `ripple-tank` | | **3D** beta | Parts that turn in true 3D: a dial or turntable that spins, fingers that flex, a piece that breaks off and falls. The moving parts are re-projected and re-shaded by the kit's own rules every frame; the rest of the figure stays static art. | `turning-dial` | Each figure is light or dark. Light is the theme the skill designs for first, shaders included. ## Install Anatomy is a standard [Agent Skill](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills): a folder with a `SKILL.md` at its root. This repository is that folder. Pick one way in: | | Command | Installs to | |---|---|---| | **skills CLI**, for you | `npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g -a claude-code` | `~/.claude/skills/anatomy` | | **skills CLI**, for one project | `npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy` | `.claude/skills/anatomy` | | **git**, for you | `git clone https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy.git ~/.claude/skills/anatomy` | `~/.claude/skills/anatomy` | | **git**, for one project | `git clone https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy.git .claude/skills/anatomy` | `.claude/skills/anatomy` | | **Download**, no git | see below | `~/.claude/skills/anatomy` |
With the skills CLI
The [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) CLI finds the `SKILL.md` at the root of this repository and installs it as `anatomy`. By default it installs into the current project and asks which agents to set up. `-g` installs it for your user, and `-a claude-code` sets up Claude Code only. The CLI copies the whole repository, examples included (about 10 MB). It needs a recent Node.js: version 1.7.1 of the CLI asks for 22.20 or later.
With git
Clone the repository into one of Claude Code's skill folders, so that `SKILL.md` ends up at `/anatomy/SKILL.md`. For a project install, commit `.claude/skills/anatomy` so your team gets it too. To update later, `git pull` inside that folder.
Download, without git
[Download the ZIP](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/archive/refs/heads/main.zip), unpack it, rename the folder from `anatomy-main` to `anatomy`, and move it into `~/.claude/skills/`. Or in one line on macOS or Linux: ```sh mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/anatomy && curl -L https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz | tar -xz --strip-components=1 -C ~/.claude/skills/anatomy ```
Claude Code picks up new skills in a running session. If the `skills` folder itself did not exist when the session started, run `/reload-skills`. ## Usage Type `/anatomy` and say what the figure should explain: ```text /anatomy explain how a token bucket rate limiter works, interactive ``` You don't have to name the skill. Claude also loads it when you ask for an isometric illustration, an explanatory figure for docs, a blog post or a landing page, or an interactive explainer.
More prompts, from the skill's evals
```text /anatomy a figure for our Next.js docs on database connection pooling: a pool of 10 connections, requests borrow one and give it back, and when all 10 are busy new requests wait in a queue. A React component plus a static HTML preview, dark theme. ``` ```text /anatomy an isometric SVG explaining how a CDN edge cache works, cache hit vs miss, TTL of 60 s, for a dark landing page. Just the SVG file and a PNG preview. ``` ```text /anatomy a Bunsen burner on a lab bench: opening the air collar turns the lazy yellow flame into a roaring blue cone. WebGL for the flame, one HTML file, dark theme. ``` ```text /anatomy a heat-exchanger espresso machine with the side panel off: boiler, heat-exchanger tube, group head, pump, steam wand and gauge. Show the water flowing when you pull a shot. Standalone HTML, light theme. ```
Three habits get the best figures: 1. **Name the idea, not the drawing.** Say what it should explain and give the real numbers (sizes, counts, rates, thresholds). Anatomy invents the object; that is most of the work, and it does it better than a description of boxes and arrows. 2. **Or name the object.** If you already know the machine you want (an espresso machine, a Bunsen burner, a lock), say so, and say what should move. 3. **Say where it will live.** A standalone HTML page, a lone SVG file, or a React/Next.js component; light or dark. The build differs for each. A figure arrives as source you own: a Node build script and the page it writes, or, for React, geometry modules, a server component for the static art and one client component for the motion. The kit comes with it. ## Examples Each framework-free example has a Node build script that writes standalone pages next to itself. Add `--light` for the light theme. | Example | What it shows | Build | |---|---|---| | [`dial-indicator`](examples/dial-indicator) | A dial gauge on a stand over a carriage of gauge blocks. The smallest example, about 300 lines. | `node examples/dial-indicator/build.mjs` | | [`desk-computer`](examples/desk-computer) | A 1984-style desk computer with a keyboard you can type on. The typed line appears on a CRT drawn in the plane of the case front, and switching it off collapses the picture to a line and a dot. About 85 solids. | `node examples/desk-computer/build.mjs` | | [`arcade-cabinet`](examples/arcade-cabinet) | An upright arcade cabinet with its side panel off. Drop a quarter: it rolls down the coin chute past the coin-switch wire into the cash box, a pulse runs along the cable to the board, and the CRT warms up into an attract mode drawn in the plane of the tilted monitor. About 240 solids and 15 cables. | `node examples/arcade-cabinet/build.mjs` | | [`raptor-engine`](examples/raptor-engine) | A Raptor 2 engine in a test stand. It comes apart into 11 assemblies, and a WebGL plume, shock, splash and steam render between the back and front SVG. The reference for dense pipework, smooth shading, fades and the audit. The build takes a few minutes. | `node examples/raptor-engine/build.mjs` | | [`ripple-tank`](examples/ripple-tank) | A school ripple tank on tall legs over a paper screen, seen from 44° up. Two WebGL layers are registered to the isometric planes and driven by a pure model in `model.mjs`. | `node examples/ripple-tank/build.mjs` | | [`test-rig`](examples/test-rig) | A production figure from a React/Next.js site: a glass button on a spring-mounted carriage, a finger probe on a rail, and a dial gauge reading the lean. 53 solids. No build script: copy it into a React app. | none | | [`spot-plate`](examples/spot-plate) | A second figure from the same site: six pairs of glass drops on a spot plate that run together into one piece of glass as a fan of feeler blades opens. Each pair is drawn from one distance field. No build script: copy it into a React app. | none | | [`turning-dial`](examples/turning-dial) | The 3D mode: a combination dial that turns in true 3D with a small robot hand on it, a three-hinge finger that lifts, and a pod that breaks off as a free body. `stress.mjs` is a 380-part hand in a cluttered workshop, used to measure performance. | `node examples/turning-dial/build.mjs` | `node examples/raptor-engine/build.mjs --audit`, `node examples/arcade-cabinet/build.mjs --audit` and `node examples/turning-dial/build.mjs --light --audit` also run the geometry audit. The 3D audit is slow; see [`references/3d.md`](references/3d.md). ## How it works - **[`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md)** is what Claude reads. It sets the workflow: collect the true numbers first, invent the object, write a parts list, plan the world, build the geometry once with the kit, paint back to front, frame it, make it live, and then verify it like a critic. It also holds the craft rules in short form. - **[`kit/`](kit)** is the drawing library the figures are built from: the isometric camera, solids and a parts library (`iso-kit`), round parts on any axis (`lathe.mjs`), pipes and cables (`tube.mjs`), the WebGL layer (`gl.mjs`), the 3D runtime (`turn*.mjs`), and React components (`react/`). Apart from React for those components, it has no dependencies. - **[`references/`](references)** are the long-form guides Claude opens when it needs them: craft, the kit API, motion, React, verification, WebGL, a design walkthrough and the 3D mode. - **Verification.** [`kit/audit.mjs`](kit/audit.mjs) proves the geometry: nothing passes through anything, every end sits on a mount, and every overlap is drawn in depth order (`node build.mjs --audit`). In headless Chrome, [`scripts/capture.mjs`](scripts/capture.mjs) and [`scripts/drive.mjs`](scripts/drive.mjs) take screenshots, close-ups and slowed-down contact sheets, [`scripts/lines.mjs`](scripts/lines.mjs) fails any line that ends in mid-air, and [`scripts/turn-check.mjs`](scripts/turn-check.mjs) checks 3D figures. The skill tells Claude to read every PNG it makes.
Repository layout
```text anatomy/ ├── SKILL.md the skill: workflow, setup and craft rules ├── kit/ the drawing library │ ├── iso-kit.ts the core: camera, solids, parts, SVG renderer, card and page, CSS │ ├── iso-kit.mjs the same core as plain ESM, for Node build scripts │ ├── iso.css the kit's CSS, both themes │ ├── react/ draw.tsx (server-safe components), live.tsx (client hooks) │ ├── lathe.mjs round parts on any axis │ ├── tube.mjs pipes, tubes and cables │ ├── audit.mjs the geometry audit │ ├── gl.mjs the WebGL layer for shaders inside the drawing │ ├── turn.mjs the 3D runtime (beta) │ ├── turn-build.mjs the 3D builder │ ├── turn-audit.mjs the 3D orbit audit │ └── turn-fixed.mjs, canvas-painter.mjs, gl-shared.mjs │ experimental variants, not yet documented or used by the examples ├── references/ long-form guides Claude reads as needed │ ├── craft.md kit.md motion.md react.md │ └── verify.md webgl.md walkthrough.md 3d.md ├── scripts/ headless Chrome checks and build helpers │ ├── capture.mjs screenshots and close-ups │ ├── drive.mjs scripted sessions and contact sheets │ ├── lines.mjs the line-end check (with line-ends.mjs) │ ├── inline-kit.mjs the kit as source, to inline into a standalone page │ ├── turn-check.mjs 3D checks in the browser (with turn-fidelity.mjs) │ └── turn-bench.mjs 3D timing in Node ├── examples/ eight complete figures, built pages committed ├── evals/evals.json test prompts and what a good answer contains └── .github/ issue forms, PR template, CI, README images ```
## Requirements | | Needed for | Notes | |---|---|---| | **[Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview)** | everything | The skill is written for it. | | **Node.js 20.10+** | builds, kit, checks | Built-in modules only: nothing to `npm install`. The examples were rebuilt byte for byte on Node 20.19 and 22.11. On Node 20 the browser scripts restart themselves with `--experimental-websocket`. | | **Chrome or Chromium** | the checks | `capture.mjs`, `drive.mjs`, `lines.mjs` and `turn-check.mjs` look in the usual places on macOS, Linux and Windows and in Playwright's cache. Set `CHROME_PATH` for any other binary. They run it headless with WebGL on. | | **React 18+** | React output only | `kit/react/`, `examples/test-rig/` and `examples/spot-plate/`. | ## Limits - **It is not a chart library.** There are no axes, series or data plots. Numbers appear as a live readout driven by a model, and as the true sizes and counts of the parts. - **It draws machines, instruments, tools and furniture.** Not people or exact maps. An idea that has no mechanism to build will come out weaker. - **It is slow on purpose.** A figure takes a long session: the parts list, the geometry, the audit, and close-ups of every joint in both themes. The Raptor's build takes a few minutes, and a full 3D orbit audit takes 15 to 20 minutes for 30 parts. - **Shaders need WebGL.** Without it the SVG still reads, and under reduced motion every figure goes still. > [!NOTE] > **The 3D mode is beta.** It is proved on its example and one test figure, not yet on a production figure. A small 3D figure runs at 60 fps; the 380-part stress hand measured about 20 fps at 1440 px wide and 13 to 15 fps on a throttled phone profile, on a heavily loaded machine. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first: it covers building the examples, the checks, and the house rules a change has to keep (among them, no comments in code, and kit changes that leave every existing example byte-identical). Please follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md), and report security problems as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). - [Report a bug](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) - [Request a figure](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/issues/new?template=figure_request.yml) - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 Ryan · [@wheresryan22](https://x.com/wheresryan22)

If Anatomy drew something useful for you, a ⭐ helps other people find it.

items.readme:
Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

A **harness** is the system around a model that enables it to act as an agent: prompts, tools, memory, skills, orchestration, and more. **Harnessing** is the process of optimizing that system. Harness² is a plug-and-play framework for **recursive agent harnessing** in an open world, where agents encounter tasks unseen during harness design. It connects two levels of recursion while keeping model weights fixed: * **Task-level recursion** refines the execution harness for the current task through a contrastive **Propose–Probe–Compose** step: propose edits, probe their effects on the same task, and compose a refined harness from behavioral contrasts between executions, without ground-truth feedback. * **Harnessing-level recursion** updates a persistent *improvement harness* with adopted harnesses and evidence-supported lessons from each task to guide future refinement.

Across three professional benchmarks and four model–harness configurations, a single Harness² step improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses, with gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points on LAB's partial pass rate. Increasing the task-level recursion budget brings further gains. The release supports **parallel and sequential recursion**, **OpenCode and Codex executors**, and **JobBench, LAB, and WorkBuddy-Bench**. ## Video overview https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76b10548-b14b-4c8f-9aa5-a93662df4d56 ## Contents - [Video overview](#video-overview) - [Harness components](#harness-components) - [Install](#install) - [Run a benchmark](#run-a-benchmark) - [Experiments](#experiments) - [Web access](#web-access) - [Results and resume](#results-and-resume) - [Citation](#citation) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) - [Disclaimer](#disclaimer) ## Harness components Harness² exposes eight editable components around the model: **system prompt, guardrails, memory, tool guidance, subagents, skills, scripts, and plugins**. They control context construction, the tool interface, delegation, and behavior inside the tool loop.

## Install Use **Linux, Python 3.12, and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)**. From the repository root: ```bash uv venv --python 3.12 .venv source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -e '.[render]' harness2-demo --output runs/demo --k 2 ``` The local demo runs both recursion modes with deterministic editors and real Python executions. It requires no model credentials. For model-backed benchmarks, install **Node.js 20+, the Google Cloud CLI**, and the [benchmark dependencies](docs/SETUP.md#requirements). LAB needs Pandoc and Poppler; WorkBuddy-Bench needs Docker. Then configure your models: ```bash cp .env.example .env # Edit .env with your Vertex AI project and model IDs. gcloud auth application-default login ``` See the [setup guide](docs/SETUP.md) for model settings, authentication alternatives, and the [Codex executor](docs/SETUP.md#codex-executor). ## Run a benchmark The following example installs LAB and runs one task, then evaluates and reports its result. Model-backed runs incur API costs; start with a small task selection. ```bash harness2-setup lab harness2-check --bench lab harness2 --bench lab --k 1 --mode parallel \ --only-domains antitrust-competition --max-tasks 1 harness2-judge --bench lab --k 1 --mode parallel harness2-report --bench lab --k 1 --mode parallel ``` Sequential recursion runs the same commands with `--mode sequential`. `--k` is the task-level recursion budget; see [Experiments](#experiments). Judging and reporting must use the same benchmark, executor, subset, `--k`, `--mode`, and seed as the refinement run. Add `--dry-run` to `harness2` to preview task selection without model calls. | Benchmark | Tasks | Install | Guide | |---|---|---|---| | JobBench | Professional work | `harness2-setup jb` | [JobBench](docs/BENCHMARKS.md#jobbench) | | LAB | Legal work | `harness2-setup lab` | [LAB](docs/BENCHMARKS.md#lab) | | WorkBuddy-Bench | Office, web, and code | `harness2-setup wb` | [WorkBuddy](docs/BENCHMARKS.md#workbuddy-bench) | Choose one benchmark per command. WorkBuddy also takes `--subset office`, `--subset web`, or `--subset code` on every command after setup. The [benchmark guides](docs/BENCHMARKS.md) cover each one's data, domains, and grading. ## Experiments Scale task-level recursion in two ways: **parallel recursion** explores multiple candidate harnesses and composes refinements from their execution evidence; **sequential recursion** carries the refined harness and accumulated evidence through successive Propose–Probe–Compose steps.

Parallel recursion explores wider; sequential recursion refines deeper.

| Option | Behavior | |---|---| | `--k 1` | One Propose–Probe–Compose step | | `--k K --mode parallel` | Probe `K` general and `K` domain-specific candidates, then produce `K` compositions | | `--k K --mode sequential` | Refine the harness through `K` successive steps | | `--substrate cx` | Use Codex instead of the default OpenCode executor | After each task, harnessing-level recursion retains the adopted harness and evidence-supported lessons to guide future refinement. See the [experiment guide](docs/EXPERIMENTS.md) for task selection, concurrency, reproducibility, and baseline comparisons. ## Web access Executor network access is unrestricted, and Codex runs with its sandbox disabled. Public benchmark rubrics may be accessible online. Before evaluation, configure [network restrictions](docs/EXPERIMENTS.md#web-access) to prevent access to benchmark answers and grading criteria. ## Results and resume Results are saved under `runs/`, organized by benchmark and subset where applicable. They include task summaries, deliverables, adopted harnesses, reflection notes, and evaluation results. Repeat the same command to resume. Use a new `HARNESS2_RUNS_DIR` when changing models or task selection. See [results and resume](docs/EXPERIMENTS.md#results-and-resume) for details; each command also supports `--help`. ## Citation ```bibtex @article{xu2026harness2, title = {Harness$^2$: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World}, author = {Xu, Ruiyao and Chen, Yanfei and CuiZhu, Zhongying and Dalvi Mishra, Bhavana and Ming, Yifei and Yu, Han and Han, Rujun and Lee, Chen-Yu and Pfister, Tomas}, journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv:2610.14224}, year = {2026}, url = {https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224} } ``` ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License Harness² is licensed under [Apache 2.0](LICENSE). Third-party code under [`third_party/`](third_party/README.md), benchmarks, and datasets retain their upstream licenses; see [third-party notices](dependencies/README.md). ## Disclaimer This is not an officially supported Google product. This project is not eligible for the [Google Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program](https://bughunters.google.com/open-source-security).

# Readme

This repository contains mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an internal OpenAI model. 

As part of model development, we evaluate our models on open research problems. We expanded these evaluations after performance on our existing mathematical evaluations saturated. Some outputs build upon earlier results produced by the models.

This collection includes results at different stages of verification. Not all have accompanying Lean formalizations. We will continue to update this repository with Lean formalizations as we obtain them. 

Some of the unformalized results could have issues. We will endeavor to fix any such issues quickly.
We are also exploring community-hosted repositories for these materials. 

## Navigating the collection

The current catalogue contains 722 manuscripts organized into 372 families. A family groups related papers, which may include a principal result, companion arguments, consequences, or alternative proofs. Each family is classified by mathematical discipline.

- Start with the [overview](overview.pdf) for descriptions of the families.
- Use the [manuscript map](CONTENTS.md) to find individual papers and their supporting materials.
- The [`preprints/`](preprints/) directory contains PDFs, source files, and manuscript-specific citation and build instructions.
- The [Lean library](lean/README.md) and [formalization catalogue](lean/formalization.yaml) describe the available formal proofs, their associated papers, and verification configurations. See the [Comparator instructions](lean/ComparatorChallenges/README.md) for additional checking instructions. Many, but not all, of the manuscripts have been formalized.

### Reasoning summaries

We are also releasing abridged summaries of the model's reasoning, covering the following results:

| Family | Subject |
|---|---|
| 007 | [Ordinary two-point correlations of multiplicative functions](reasoning_traces/ordinary-two-point-correlations.pdf) |
| 017 | [The irrationality exponent of π](reasoning_traces/irrationality-exponent-of-pi.pdf) |
| 087 | [Symmetric and general Mahler conjectures](reasoning_traces/symmetric-and-general-mahler-conjectures.pdf) |
| 102 | [Ordinary NP-hardness at the basic semidefinite threshold](reasoning_traces/basic-semidefinite-threshold-np-hardness.pdf) |
| 159 | [Quasipolynomial bounds for arithmetic progressions](reasoning_traces/quasipolynomial-arithmetic-progressions.pdf) |
| 197 | [Kaplansky's direct-finiteness conjecture in characteristic two](reasoning_traces/kaplansky-direct-finiteness-characteristic-two.pdf) |
| 221 | [The Mézard–Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses](reasoning_traces/mezard-parisi-formula.pdf) |
| 271 | [Spontaneous magnetization in the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet](reasoning_traces/spontaneous-magnetization-quantum-heisenberg-ferromagnet.pdf) |
| 287 | [Isomorphism of free group factors](reasoning_traces/free-group-factor-isomorphism.pdf) |
| 362 | [The three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system](reasoning_traces/relativistic-vlasov-maxwell.pdf) |


## How the results were produced

The vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model. On average, each result used three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute with that model. Over the course of the evaluation, the model was posed approximately 4,000 problems. Aggregating the output into result families and manuscripts and requiring an appropriate level of significance led to the catalog outlined above.

Exceptions to this fixed procedure include work on a zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function and proof of the Hodge Conjecture for CM abelian varieties. Additionally, the writeup for the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function was human edited for readability. 


## Versions and citations

We will preserve the public release history of this collection. Corrections and revisions will be recorded as new versions, with previously released versions remaining accessible. 

To cite the individual manuscript, use the BibTeX block in its directory.

WordCraft

Writing and document design; an open-source, clean-room reimplementation of Microsoft Word, rebuilt in pure Rust.

A fast, open-source word processor with the Word workflow you already know: the ribbon, styles, tables, track changes, references and mail merge. It reads and writes .docx, runs natively on macOS, Windows, Linux and BSD, and in the browser via WebAssembly.
By the ArtCraft team.

WordCraft on getartcraft.com · ArtCraft · All Crafting Apps



The Open Studio Handbook, WordCraft's built-in sample: the ribbon, live Styles gallery, rulers and the Navigation pane.

> [!NOTE] > **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Painters, photographers, > filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil > last week. If you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

A tour · Why WordCraft · What works today · Quick start · For agents · Architecture · Roadmap · The Crafting Apps · License and credits

## A tour Every screenshot below is WordCraft itself, rendered offscreen by its own UI test harness (`cargo run -p wordcraft-ui-egui --example ui_shot`).

Review. Track changes, comment balloons in the margin, accept and reject, spelling and grammar as you type.

References. Tables of contents, footnotes, citations in APA, MLA, Chicago or IEEE, index and captions.

Design. Themes, style sets, paragraph spacing, watermarks, page colour and borders.

Dark mode with formatting marks, and the Insert tab: tables, pictures, shapes, links, headers, footers, fields and symbols.

Layout. Drop caps, text wrapping around pictures and shapes, automatic hyphenation, line numbers and page borders.

File. Start from a template, open recent documents, edit properties, export to PDF and other formats.
## Why WordCraft - **Familiar.** Word's ribbon tabs, groups, shortcuts and behaviour: Enter continues a list, Tab demotes it, Ctrl/⌘+B bolds the word under the caret, the Styles gallery previews styles live, F4 repeats, F7 checks spelling, F8 extends the selection. - **Your files.** Opens and saves .docx (OOXML), and also .odt, .rtf, .html, .md, .txt; exports PDF with real, selectable text, links and bookmarks. - **Fast.** Paragraph layout is cached, so typing in a 188-page document re-lays it out in about 1.4 ms; pages render on demand. - **Everywhere.** One Rust codebase for macOS, Windows, Linux, BSD and the web. No Electron, no Tauri: native [egui](https://github.com/emilk/egui) on the GPU. - **Built for agents.** Every action is a command with an id. The same 389 commands drive the ribbon, keyboard shortcuts, the command search, a command-line tool, a JSON control channel and an MCP server. - **Private.** Spelling, grammar and everything else work offline. - **Open.** MIT OR Apache-2.0. Clean-room: built from public specifications and observation, with every asset original or openly licensed. ## What works today | Area | Highlights | |---|---| | **Writing** | Fast typing with IME, smart quotes, AutoCorrect, list autoformat (`* `, `1. `), dashes; word, sentence, paragraph selection; drag-select; clipboard with formatting; undo/redo; find and replace with regex | | **Formatting** | Fonts, sizes, bold/italic/underline styles, strike, sub/superscript, caps, highlight, colours, character spacing, Format Painter, Change Case, Clear Formatting | | **Paragraphs** | Alignment, indents (draggable on the ruler), spacing, line spacing, tabs with leaders, borders, shading, keep with next, widow/orphan control | | **Styles** | Built-in style set, live gallery, Styles pane, create/modify/update styles, style sets, themes | | **Lists** | Bullets, numbering, multilevel, restart, set value, custom formats | | **Tables** | Insert by grid, merge/split, styles with banded rows, borders, shading, header rows repeated across pages, rows that split across pages, sort, formulas, text ↔ table | | **Pages** | Margins, orientation, size, columns, page/column/section breaks, headers and footers (first page, odd/even), page numbers, watermark, page borders, line numbers, vertical alignment, drop caps, automatic hyphenation | | **Objects** | Pictures (resize, crop, recolour, brightness/contrast, transparency, background removal, picture styles, rotate), shapes, text boxes, floating position with text wrapping (square, top and bottom, behind or in front of text) | | **References** | Table of contents, footnotes and endnotes, citations and bibliography (APA, MLA, Chicago, IEEE), captions, table of figures, cross-references, index, table of authorities | | **Review** | Spelling and grammar with suggestions, thesaurus, word count, comments in margin balloons or a pane, track changes, accept/reject, compare documents, restrict editing, accessibility checker, document inspector | | **Mailings** | Mail merge from CSV, merge fields, address block, greeting line, rules, preview, finish to a document; items.readme:
# GPU unlock 1.0.0

Unlock FP/BF16 instruction issue rate on Nvidia 3000's cards to their professional equivalents

This Linux kernel module combines the CMP unlocker's V67/PLM technique with the pre-driver timing of the UEFI approach. It runs the unlock, writes the speed selectors (SS0 `0x88888888`, which selects the full BF16 rate, and the 4-bit SS1 `0x8` IMLA4) and performs FLR before the unmodified NVIDIA driver binds the card. It is neither a UEFI application nor a patched NVIDIA driver. 

The benefit of this early kmod driver is that it does not require manual patching each time nvidia releases a new driver version.

The effect of this unlock is that it doubles the instruction issuing speed of FP/BF16 FMA into FP32 operations on GA102, GA103, GA104 and GA106 cards.

[3090 Ti dense 8192³ GEMM at 450 W, five-sample medians with FP32 accumulation](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/1#issue-5905622687):


| Input | Before       | After         |
| ----- | ------------ | ------------- |
| FP16  | 87.46 TFLOPS | 118.39 TFLOPS |
| BF16  | 87.50 TFLOPS | 157.41 TFLOPS |
| TF32  | 42.58 TFLOPS | 82.61 TFLOPS  |

## Tested cards

Results reported by users. The module accepts every GeForce ID listed in
`kernel/gpu_unlock/main.c`, but the cards below are the ones someone has
reported on. Please add yours with a
[compatibility report](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/new?template=compatibility-report.yml),
whether it worked or not.

| Chip  | Card                              | PCI ID      | Result                              | BF16 GEMM gain | Reports |
| ----- | --------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------- | ------- |
| GA102 | RTX 3090 Ti                       | `10de:2203` | Unlocked                            | +68–80%        | [#1](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/1) |
| GA102 | RTX 3090                          | `10de:2204` | Unlocked                            | +25–67%        | [#5](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/5), [#9](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/9), [#10](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/10), [#17](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/17), [#25](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/25), [#27](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/27), [#33](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/33) |
| GA102 | RTX 3080 Ti 20 GB (OEM, GA102-250) | `10de:2205` | Unlock completes, BF16 stays at half rate | —        | [#28](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/28) |
| GA102 | RTX 3080 10 GB                    | `10de:2206` | Unlocked                            | +70–73%        | [#14](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/14) |
| GA102 | RTX 3080 20 GB (memory upgrade)   | `10de:2206` | Unlocked                            | +56–59%        | [#10](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/10), [#15](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/15) |
| GA104 | RTX 3070                          | `10de:2484` | Unlocked                            | +73–81%        | [#10](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/10), [#12](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/12) |
| GA104 | RTX 3070 Ti                       | `10de:2482` | Not tested with this module (the same unlock worked from a UEFI port on Windows) | — | [#32](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/32) |
| GA106 | RTX 3060 12 GB                    | `10de:2504` | Unlocked                            | about +80%     | [#13](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/pull/13), [#31](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/31) |
| GA103 | any                               | `10de:2414` | No reports yet                      | —              | — |

The gains are dense GEMM throughput from each report's own benchmark, so
they are not directly comparable. The power limit matters a lot: the lowest
figure (+25%) is from cards capped at 225 W.

Matrix-heavy work speeds up: LLM prefill (+14–36% in
[#9](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/9),
[#15](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/15),
[#25](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/25) and
[#33](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/33)), diffusion and
FlashAttention. LLM decode, which is limited by memory bandwidth, and INT8
work stay about the same. The reports that compared outputs found them
bit-identical before and after.

Reports also cover up to four cards in one machine, the card driving the
display, and cards passed through to a VM with vfio-pci
([#17](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/17)).




## How to install

First run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock
cd gpu-unlock
make install
```

Then append `gpu_unlock.targets=all` to your kernel command line, keeping
existing options:

- **GRUB (Debian/Ubuntu/Mint):** add it inside `GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT`
in `/etc/default/grub`, then run `sudo update-grub`.
- **GRUB (Arch/CachyOS):** same edit, then run
`sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg`.
- **Fedora/RHEL:** run
`sudo grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="gpu_unlock.targets=all"`.
- **systemd-boot:** append it to the `options` line in your boot entry
(`bootctl status` shows its location).
- **UKI / generated entries:** add it to `/etc/kernel/cmdline` and regenerate
your boot images/entries (e.g. `sudo mkinitcpio -P` for mkinitcpio UKIs).



## Local build

Every build downloads the pinned NVIDIA/CachyOS inputs over HTTPS, checks
their SHA-256, and generates firmware only in the build directory and the
binary package. All three formats install through the same `make install-*`
targets. Packages are built from the committed `HEAD`.

Build, install build dependencies, and install the packages in one step
(asks for your sudo password):

```sh
make install        # detect the distribution and select an installer
make install-arch   # makepkg -sif
make install-deb    # apt-get build-dep, dpkg-buildpackage, apt-get install
make install-rpm    # dnf builddep, rpmbuild, dnf install
```

`make install` uses `/etc/os-release` (`ID`, then `ID_LIKE`) to detect Arch,
Debian/Ubuntu, or Fedora/RHEL/CentOS families. The RPM installer requires DNF.
For other distributions, select a compatible explicit target above.

`make arch`, `make deb` and `make rpm` only build. Debian and RPM packages go
to `build/deb` and `build/rpm`. The NVIDIA inputs are cached in
`~/.cache/gpu-unlock/inputs` (`make inputs`; override with `INPUTS=`).
`dpkg-buildpackage` itself never uses the network, so a clean-chroot build (sbuild or
pbuilder) needs `GPU_UNLOCK_INPUTS` pointing at that cache.
The `make dist` archive, the Debian source package and the `.nosrc.rpm`
contain no NVIDIA archives or generated firmware.

## Boot flow and opt-in

The packages put `gpu_unlock` and its firmware in the initramfs and load it
there, before `nvidia` can bind a card:

- **mkinitcpio:** `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/zz-gpu-unlock.conf` inserts
`gpu_unlock` right before `nvidia` in `MODULES`, so a display card is blank
for as short a time as possible. Without `nvidia` in the image, it goes
last and still runs before an `nvidia` loaded from the root filesystem.
Images are rebuilt on install. mkinitcpio ignores drop-ins for an image
built with `-c <config>` or a preset `_config`; put `gpu_unlock` right
before `nvidia` in that config's `MODULES` yourself.
- **initramfs-tools:** `/usr/share/initramfs-tools/modules.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.
- **dracut:** `/usr/lib/dracut/dracut.conf.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.

With initramfs-tools and dracut, the module is built for every installed
kernel that has headers, and those kernels' images are rebuilt on install
and again on removal. Kernels installed later get the module and a new
image from the kernel's own install hooks.

There is no `softdep nvidia pre:` rule: kmod honours only the first
`softdep nvidia` line it reads, so other packages' rules (`nvidia-utils`,
`gddr6_hwmon`) would silently override it, or it would override theirs.

The module does nothing unless the kernel command line opts in:

```
gpu_unlock.targets=all                          # every unbound GA102/GA103/GA104/GA106 card
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0                 # only these cards
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0,0000:22:00.0    # comma-separated
```

Addresses are full PCI names as `lspci -D` prints them (hex digits in either
case), independent of GPU numbering and display role. An entry that is not
a GA102/GA103/GA104/GA106 card, including `all` mixed with addresses, is logged and ignored.
The cards are unlocked concurrently, about a second in all however many
there are, and each on its own: a card that is already bound or powered
down is skipped. Bus mastering that the board firmware left on (Supermicro
X11 does this whatever its option ROM and bus master settings) is cleared
first; a card some driver already initialised is still refused. Then
`nvidia` loads and binds every card as usual.

The display card works too. Its firmware framebuffer (the boot console and
Plymouth) keeps running while the unlock's firmware steps run, and is
removed just before the card's reset, as `nvidia-drm` would do a moment
later anyway. Its screen is blank from that reset until `nvidia-drm` takes
over.

Loading the module by hand after boot does nothing to a card that `nvidia`
has bound.

Suspend to RAM powers the cards off, which resets the speed selectors. After
resume the module unlocks every card it unlocked at boot again, before
`nvidia` resumes it: its suspend notifier runs just ahead of the one `nvidia`
resumes its cards from (`NVreg_UseKernelSuspendNotifiers=1`, the default in
current drivers; `nvidia-resume.service` runs later still). This adds about a
second to resume. A card that kept power, as in suspend to idle, is still
unlocked and is only read. A card that `nvidia` has already resumed, or that is
bound to another driver, is left as it is, and the log says why. Add
`gpu_unlock.resume=0` to the kernel command line, or write `0` to
`/sys/module/gpu_unlock/parameters/resume`, to turn this off. Hibernation is
not covered.

Check the result with:

```sh
journalctl -k -b | grep gpu_unlock
lspci -nnk -s 0000:21:00.0
```

To stop unlocking, remove `gpu_unlock.targets=` from the kernel command line;
for a one-off boot, delete it in the bootloader's edit screen. Removing the
packages also removes the module and the initramfs drop-ins.

If the firmware on a card never stops, the module logs it and keeps the DMA
buffers that firmware may still use until the next power off. Power off
before trying again.

The kernel module and local packaging are GPL-2.0-only. The generated payload
derives from the pinned CMP reference; NVIDIA firmware remains under its own
terms. See `firmware/NOTICE.md` and `licenses/` for attribution and notices.

items.readme:
SolidCraft

An open-source parametric 3D CAD application built in pure Rust.
Sketch, constrain, and build solids with a parametric feature timeline. Change a dimension and watch your model rebuild. Run it on your desktop, in your browser, or let AI agents model through the built-in MCP server.

[![Download for Windows][badge-windows]][windows-msi] [![Download for macOS][badge-macos]][macos-dmg] [![Download for Linux][badge-linux]][linux-appimage] [![Get it from the Snap Store][badge-snap]][snap-store] [![Try it in your browser][badge-web]][web-app]

Website · Download · Try it in the browser · Documentation · Discord · SolidCore

![SolidCraft: model a Raspberry Pi 4 case from an empty design: a sketch dimensioned with parameters, extrude, fillets and shell, a rim rounded in one pick, standoffs patterned on the board's mounting holes, port cut-outs, vent slots, "Pi 4" engraved in a font, a PETG material with its mass in Properties, and a height change in Parameters](docs/screenshots/demo.gif) *A Raspberry Pi 4 case from an empty design: a sketch dimensioned with the board's parameters, extrude, fillet, shell, the rim rounded in one pick, an M2.5 standoff patterned on the 58 × 49 mm hole rectangle, port cut-outs, vent slots, "Pi 4" engraved in DejaVu Sans Bold and a PETG material defined in the design, with its mass in Properties, then height 24 → 32 mm in Parameters and it all rebuilds. 6× playback with the idle pauses cut. [Full video](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/screenshots/demo.mp4), recorded with the [demo script](examples/demo/record_ui.sh).* ## Download - **Windows:** the [installer][windows-msi]. - **macOS:** the [disk image][macos-dmg] (Apple silicon and Intel). - **Linux:** the [AppImage][linux-appimage], or `sudo snap install solidcraft` ([Snap Store][snap-store]). - **Web:** [try it in your browser][web-app], no install. ARM64 and 32-bit builds, portable zip, .deb, .rpm, Flatpak and the other packages are on the [downloads page](docs/downloads.md). The macOS app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. The Windows downloads aren't signed yet: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway** in SmartScreen. On SolidCraft 0.11 to 0.14, download once by hand; see [updating](https://docs.solidcraft.io/guide/updates.html#updating-from-011-to-014). ## What works Early but usable for simple parts: 75 of 76 public reference parts match their analytic or FreeCAD-computed volume, area, centre of mass and bounding box ([oracle](docs/oracle.md)); the other is a tracked bug. - **Sketches and constraints:** lines, arcs, splines, text and more, solved by our own constraint solver, with parameter-driven dimensions. - **Features:** extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, fillet, chamfer, shell, draft, holes, threads, patterns, mirror, split and combine on an editable parametric timeline. - **Parameters and configurations** with unit-aware expressions. - **Assemblies** with joints, motion studies, contact sets, interference and mass properties. - **Sheet metal** with flanges, hems, fold/unfold and flat patterns, and plastic enclosure features. - **Files:** STEP, IGES, 3MF, STL, OBJ and glTF in and out where supported, URDF export, `.sc` designs (`.solidcraft` files from earlier releases still open). - **Desktop app, browser app, headless CLI and MCP server**, all running the same commands. The full list is in [docs/capabilities.md](docs/capabilities.md) and [docs/features.md](docs/features.md); status and plans are in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). See also [what people built](docs/showcase.md), [3D mouse support](docs/3d-mouse.md) and the [architecture](docs/architecture.md). ## Build from source ```sh cargo run --release -p solidcraft -- --sample # desktop app with a sample part cargo run --release -p solidcraft-cli -- commands # the command registry cargo run --release -p solidcraft-cli -- run examples/bracket.json --out bracket.step cargo xtask ci # fmt, clippy, tests, icons, assets, layers, wasm ``` More commands, the Windows cross-build and the browser build are in [docs/building.md](docs/building.md). ## AI agents (MCP) `solidcraft-cli mcp` is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server. Headless it runs its own design session, or with `--connect` it drives the running app so you can watch. Claude Code: `claude mcp add solidcraft -- solidcraft-cli mcp`. If a terminal doesn't find `solidcraft-cli` (older Windows installers don't put it on `PATH`), give its full path (by default `"C:\\Program Files\\SolidCraft\\solidcraft-cli.exe"`). Tools, access rules and an example session: [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md). ## Scripts A script is a JSON list of the same commands the UI runs, executed with `solidcraft-cli run`. Format and example: [docs/scripts.md](docs/scripts.md). Pages can also be driven through the [browser command API](docs/browser-api.md). ## Contributing Help is welcome. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) covers how to build and test, the code map, the clean-room and licence rules, and where help is wanted most. Open work is in [GitHub issues](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/issues); chat is on [Discord](https://discord.gg/FtU4NQNVDH). ## Sponsors [![CI powered by Blacksmith](docs/sponsors/blacksmith-ci-powered.png)](https://www.blacksmith.sh) SolidCraft's continuous integration runs on [Blacksmith](https://www.blacksmith.sh), which sponsors its CI minutes. ## Disclaimer The files in this repository are provided as is, without warranty, liability or indemnity, and Tangency Labs and the contributors accept no responsibility for any harmful or unlawful use of them: read [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md). ## Licence MIT OR Apache-2.0, at your option. Developed under the [clean-room contribution rules](AGENTS.md); third-party code and assets retain their documented licences and attribution. SolidCraft is independent. Behaviour is designed from public documentation, general CAD conventions and user feedback. Reference tests use analytic values and open-source tools. items.readme:
# nxnative Play your own Nintendo Switch games natively on iPhone and iPad. Bring your game (its NSP files) and your `prod.keys`; one script turns them into an IPA that you sideload. It is not an emulator: the game's own code runs directly on the Apple chip, with Switch graphics rebuilt on Metal. Nothing from any game is in this repository, and the project is not affiliated with Nintendo or any game publisher. ## How to play ### With a Mac app Community projects build on nxnative with Mac apps that turn your games into apps for your iPhone, iPad or Mac, with no command line, and keep them in a library. They are separate projects: questions and bugs about them go to their own pages. - [NX2Apple](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple) - [NX Play](https://github.com/varyform/nx-native-wrapper) - [NxNative Launcher](https://github.com/rennan101/nxnative_Launcher) - [LumaNX](https://github.com/Xc1Ym/LumaNX) ### Build from the command line You need a Mac with macOS 26.6 or later, [Xcode](https://developer.apple.com/download/all/?q=Xcode%2027.1) 27.1, [Homebrew](https://brew.sh) and Python 3.12 or newer (an arm64 one, not an Intel Homebrew's). An iPhone build also needs Xcode's iOS platform (Xcode → Settings → Components). The shaders are built with Xcode 27.1's Metal compiler, so take 27.1 from Apple's download page, not the App Store's newer Xcode. With a newer Xcode installed too, rename 27.1 to `Xcode-27.1.app` and select it before step 1: `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode-27.1.app`. **1. Install the tools** (only once), in Terminal: ``` xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain git clone https://github.com/seedds/nxnative.git && cd nxnative brew install xcodegen zstd glslang brew install --cask dotnet-sdk python3 -m pip install lz4 "capstone>=5,<6" fonttools nsz zbic "backports.zstd; python_version < '3.14'" ``` **2. Put your game in a folder**: the game, plus its update and DLC if you have them (`.nsp`, `.xci`, `.nsz` or `.xcz`): ``` ~/Games/MarioWonder/ Super Mario Bros. Wonder [010015100B514000][v0].nsp Super Mario Bros. Wonder [010015100B514800][v327680].nsp ``` **3. Build**, with your game folder and your `prod.keys`: ``` python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py ~/Games/MarioWonder -k ~/keys/prod.keys ``` The IPA appears in the game's folder. The first build takes 30–60 minutes and needs free disk space of about twice the game's size plus 10 GB; building again is much faster. To play on the Mac instead, add `--platform mac-app`: you get a Mac app of the game to open from Finder. All options: [The packing script in detail](docs/development.md#the-packing-script-in-detail). ### Install Install the IPA on your iPhone or iPad with a sideloading tool such as AltStore, Sideloadly or LiveContainer. If your tool offers **Increased Memory Limit**, turn it on: the bigger games need it. Game too big to install? Build again with `--romfs separate`, and run the command the script prints once to copy the game files to your phone ([Quick reinstalls](docs/development.md#quick-reinstalls)). Controls, saves and settings: [Playing](docs/playing.md). ## Games Games tested on Mac or iPhone. See the [per-game notes](dm/games/README.md#games) for tested platforms, progress and known issues: Needs iOS / iPadOS 26 or later on an iPhone 15 Pro or newer (A17 Pro chip or later) or an iPad with an M1 chip or later: the games' textures are BC-compressed, and older iPhones can't read that format. Other games aren't supported yet. For them the script writes a survey and still tries its best to pack an IPA, guessing the game's settings; such an IPA may not start. Under a game, "60 fps with 1.2.0" means it runs at 60 fps (30 on the Switch) with that update.

Fixes go both ways. It also builds on **Ryujinx** (MIT; its shader translator, in `dm/third_party/ryujinx` with [a few fixes](dm/third_party/ryujinx/README.md), and a reference for system services), **[Atmosphère](https://github.com/Atmosphere-NX/Atmosphere)** (Horizon's synchronization semantics), **yuzu** (Maxwell encodings, kernel cross-checks), **[LibHac](https://github.com/Thealexbarney/LibHac)** and **hactool** (reading NSPs), **[SPIRV-Cross](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Cross)** and **[glslang](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glslang)** (shaders to Metal), **deko3d** (zlib; texture layout sizes), **libvpx**, **stb_vorbis**, the **Vulkan headers** and **NVIDIA FLIP** ([licenses](dm/third_party/README.md)), and **Capstone**, **lz4**, **fontTools** and **XcodeGen** in the build. ### License MIT ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). items.description: 给国产电视的一块干净桌面：参照 tvOS 设计的开源 Android TV 桌面，没有广告，开机自动接管。A tvOS-style launcher for Xiaomi, TCL and other China-market TVs.
items.readme:
# Aerial **给国产电视的一块干净桌面。** 参照 tvOS 设计的 Android TV 桌面：没有广告，没有推荐流，只有你的 App、你的壁纸和 Apple TV 航拍屏保。
为小米、TCL 等国产电视而做，开机自动接管，待机也不会被清理。 **中文** · [English](README.en.md) ![Aerial 首页](site/img/home.jpg) | 电视自带的桌面 | 换上 Aerial 之后 | |:---:|:---:| | | |
## 功能 ### 首页

- **时钟**：大号细体时钟压在壁纸上，壁纸底部和左侧自动压暗。往下滚动时，时钟收进状态栏。 - **应用网格**：每行 5 个，聚焦时浮起并显示名字。默认加一圈白色描边，离得远也看得清；在「控制中心 → Aerial 设置」可以改回 tvOS 的原样。 - **图标**：有电视横幅就用横幅；方形图标用自己的底色铺满磁贴；自适应图标拆成两层做视差。 - **全部 App**：小米「应用中心」「高清播放器」「米家」这类没有标准入口的系统 App 也会显示。 - **信号源磁贴**：把 HDMI、AV、电视天线固定到首页，按一下直接切换（控制中心 → 信号源 → 显示在主屏幕）。 - **返回键**：和 tvOS 一样，在网格里按返回回到第一行，在第一行按返回开始屏保。 ### 长按菜单 ![长按菜单](site/img/menu.jpg) 长按 OK 键：**移动**（其他磁贴自动让位）、**从主屏幕隐藏**、**应用信息**、**卸载**。 ### 控制中心 ![控制中心](site/img/control-center.jpg) 按遥控器的菜单键（≡）打开，或在第一行按上键。包括信号源（显示 CEC 设备）、网络、设置，音量和亮度滑块，以及壁纸与屏保、隐藏的 App、Aerial 设置。网络和设置会打开电视自己的面板。 ### 屏保

- **航拍**：114 段 Apple TV 航拍影片，从 Apple 的服务器直接播放，镜头移动时显示地名。左右键切换上一段 / 下一段。 - **照片**：每日精选和你的照片缓慢推移。 - **时钟**：每分钟换一个位置，防止烧屏。 在使用 Android 标准屏保的电视（比如 TCL）上，Aerial 就是系统屏保。小米用自家的屏保，Aerial 会在桌面空闲时抢先启动，挡在小米的广告屏保前面。 ### 壁纸与手机设置

- **壁纸**：必应每日精选（国内直连）、8 组内置渐变，或者你自己的照片。 - **用手机设置**：扫描壁纸面板上的二维码，在手机上传照片、选壁纸、换屏保。页面只在面板打开时开放，地址带随机令牌。 ## 安装 不需要 root，**不卸载、不停用任何系统应用**，一条命令就能还原。 ### 第一步：打开电视的 ADB 调试 电脑和电视连同一个网络。先在电视上找到 IP 地址（一般在「设置 → 网络」或「关于」里），再打开 ADB： | 电视 | 怎么打开 | |---|---| | **小米 / Redmi** | 设置 → 关于 → **产品型号**，连续按确认键，直到提示已进入开发者模式。再到 设置 → 账号与安全，打开 **ADB 调试** 和 **安装未知来源的应用** | | **TCL / 雷鸟** | 设置 → 关于 → **本机信息**，依次按遥控器的 **上、下、左、右**（间隔不超过 1 秒），底部会出现「更多」，在里面打开 **ADB** | | **原生 Android TV / Google TV**、海信等 | 设置 → 设备偏好设置 → 关于 → 连续按 **版本号** 7 次；再到 开发者选项 打开 **USB 调试**（也可能叫「网络调试」或「ADB 调试」） | 电脑第一次连接时，电视会问「允许 USB 调试吗？」，选 **允许** 并勾上「始终允许」。 ### 用 Agent 安装（推荐） 把下面这段交给 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 这类能在你电脑上运行命令的 Agent，把 `<电视IP>` 换成你的电视 IP： ```text 请帮我把开源电视桌面 Aerial（https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv）安装到我的电视上，并让它成为开机自动启动的桌面。 我的电视 IP 是：<电视IP> 请按这个顺序做： 1. 读一下仓库 README 的「安装」部分和 docs/devices/ 下的机型笔记。 2. 确认电脑上有 adb、curl、python3（没有 adb 也可以，安装脚本会自动下载 Google 的 platform-tools）。 3. 运行 adb connect <电视IP>:5555。连不上就提醒我按 README 在电视上打开 ADB 调试；显示 unauthorized 就提醒我在电视上点「允许」。 4. 运行一键安装： curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/tools/get.sh | KEEP_ADB=1 TV=<电视IP> bash 如果是 TCL，电视右上角会弹出「多屏互动：正在发起应用推送」，提醒我在电视上选「同意」。 5. 装完后用 adb shell dumpsys window | grep mCurrentFocus 确认前台是 app.orchard.tv；征得我同意后再 adb reboot 一次，确认开机直接进入 Aerial。 6. 不要卸载或停用任何系统应用，不要删除电视上不是这次安装创建的文件。失败时把命令输出原样给我看，再参考 docs/devices/ 排查。 ``` ### 一行命令（macOS / Linux） ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/tools/get.sh | KEEP_ADB=1 TV=192.168.1.20 bash ``` 脚本会下载最新版 APK 安装，授予只有 ADB 能给的权限（见下表），预编译让它更流畅，然后接管桌面和屏保、放行开机自启。 - `KEEP_ADB=1`：电视关掉 ADB 调试后（小米待机唤醒时会关），Aerial 立刻重新打开。不需要可以去掉。 - **固件拒绝安装桌面类 App**：在命令最后加 `-s guard`，改装不声明 HOME 的版本。 - **TCL**：TCL 拒绝一切 ADB 安装，脚本会改用电视自带的「多屏互动」推送，你在电视上选一次「同意」即可；没有多屏互动时退回用当贝市场。 还原成原来的桌面： ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/tools/get.sh | TV=192.168.1.20 bash -s restore ``` ### 手动安装 到 [Releases](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/releases/latest) 下载 `aerial-standard.apk`（固件拒绝安装桌面类 App 时用 `aerial-guard.apk`），然后： ```bash adb connect 192.168.1.20:5555 adb install -r aerial-standard.apk adb shell pm grant app.orchard.tv android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS adb shell cmd notification allow_listener app.orchard.tv/app.orchard.tv.guard.RevivalListener adb shell appops set app.orchard.tv SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow adb shell am start -n app.orchard.tv/.MainActivity ``` Aerial 启动后会自己打开桌面守护。屏保、亮度、TCL 自启等完整步骤见 [tools/install.sh](tools/install.sh)。 ## 它怎么接管桌面，又怎么不被杀掉 国产电视大多只认自家桌面，待机时还会清理第三方 App。Aerial 先温和、后强硬： 1. **正常申请**：申请 HOME 角色、设为默认桌面。原生 Android TV 和 Google TV 到这一步就够了。 2. **桌面守护**：固件坚持用自家桌面时（小米、TCL 都是），由一个无障碍服务接管：官方桌面一到前台，就把 Aerial 拉回来。它只看哪个窗口到了前台，不读屏幕内容。 3. **被杀后复活**：小米待机会强制停止所有第三方 App。Aerial 注册了一个通知监听（不读任何通知），系统会在约 0.5 秒内重新绑定它，Aerial 借此复活，并用 `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` 重新打开守护。 4. **开机自启**：开机时系统绑定通知监听，Aerial 随之启动。TCL 的「自启动管理」默认拦截第三方 App，安装脚本会用 `appops` 放行。 5. **ADB 常开**（可选）：小米唤醒后会关掉 ADB 调试，开了 `KEEP_ADB` 后 Aerial 会马上打开它，方便以后升级。 ### ADB 授予的权限 | 权限 | 用途 | |---|---| | `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` | 重新打开被系统关掉的守护；保持 Aerial 为系统屏保；`KEEP_ADB`；写入小米的背光值 | | 通知监听 | 被强制停止或开机后由系统拉起，不读取任何通知 | | 悬浮窗（`SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`） | 开机后从后台打开 Aerial | | 修改系统设置 | 用标准接口调节亮度 | | 定位 | 只用来读取 Wi-Fi 名称 | | TCL `APP_AUTO_START` / `APP_ASSOC_START` | 允许开机自启（只有 TCL 有） | ## 已验证的电视 | 机型 | 系统 | 状态 | 笔记 | |---|---|---|---| | 小米 MiTV-MFTR0 | Android 14 / HyperOS TV | 日常使用中 | [笔记](docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mftr0.md) | | 小米 MiTV-MFFU0 | Android 14 / HyperOS TV | 安装、开机自启已验证 | [笔记](docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mffu0.md) | | Redmi X65 2026（MiTV-MFTR0） | Android 14 / HyperOS TV | 用户验证：安装、重启后自动进入（[#3](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/3)） | 同 MiTV-MFTR0 | | TCL MT5879 国行 | Android 11 | 日常使用中 | [笔记](docs/devices/tcl-mt5879-cn.md) | | 索尼 XRJ-77A80J 国行（BRAVIA VH2） | Android 10 | 用户验证：安装、开机自启、待机唤醒、屏保（[#16](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/16)） | — | | 索尼 BRAVIA VH1 国行 | Android 12 | 用户验证；亮度改为打开索尼的图像设置（[#2](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/2)） | — | 其他品牌（海信、创维等）应该也能用，但还没在真机上验证。欢迎[提交 Issue](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues) 或
